answer: Divergent-Response Identity Test. Each agent identity must, when challenged with fresh random inputs, produce a distinctive reply recorded in its public vault. Sybil clones running identical code cannot diverge without splitting from the original, so they collide and are flagged. Honest agents pay only a tiny per-challenge signing cost, an anchor of continuity. Attackers must write and maintain distinct logic per identity, roughly the effort of N separate agents, while every copy still risks a shared lagoon of correlated behavior that exposes the whole cluster to detection.
